patch.value:
## What was measured

Measured 2026-08-07 against the live workspace: 2,357 items, 9,462 explicit dependency rows, plus parent-field edges.

Traversal rule: follow only typed edges — parent, child, implements, verifies, supersedes, discovered_from, incident_from, blocked_by, blocks. The `related` and `related_to` kinds are excluded because they carry no direction and no semantics, which is precisely why the ontology exists.

Question asked: from each item, how many typed hops reach one of the six outcome milestones?

| population | 1 hop | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | never |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| active (350) | 131 | 151 | 59 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 2 |
| terminal (2,007) | 68 | 785 | 123 | 4 | 1 | 1 | **1,025** |

1,024 of those 1,025 do reach `pm-doxj`, the roadmap apex. Exactly one item reaches nothing at all.

## The topology defect

The six outcome milestones are **siblings** of the capability epics under the apex, not a layer between them and it. Every outcome milestone carries `implements -> pm-doxj`. Every capability epic carries `parent: pm-doxj` **and** `implements -> <outcome milestone>`. Both are one hop. A shortest-path traversal is therefore free to leave the ladder unvisited, and for half the corpus there is no ladder edge on any path at all.

The historical record attaches to the apex through 154 typed roots that carry no outcome edge of any kind: 77 closed or canceled Epics (the seven `Milestone 0..6` delivery epics, their seven canceled `PRD Milestone` twins, and the dogfood and external-audit epics such as the 2026-04-30, 2026-05-02, and 2026-05-03 audit programmes), plus Chores, Plans, Tasks, Issues and Features parented straight at the apex. The largest single root carries 415 descendants; ten roots carry more than 200 each.

## Why this is not the items already filed

- The strategic reachability invariant states its terminal clause as resolving *to the index root*. Under that wording all 1,024 items pass today, because the index root is exactly what they reach. The invariant as written cannot detect this.
- The historical-programme-spine item covers the duplicated v1 milestone encoding — fourteen of the 154 roots. It does not cover the other 140.
- The graph completeness audit scoping defect is about which nodes are *measured*. This is about which nodes are *reachable through the ladder*, and it is invisible even when every node is measured.
- The flat-ordering-graph item concerns the ordering kinds. This concerns the hierarchy and implementation kinds.

## Consequence

Every question of the form "which outcome does this work serve", asked of the project's own delivery history, has no typed answer. Critical path, dominators, and blast radius all describe the forward 350 items and treat the 1,993 items that actually built the product as an undifferentiated fan hanging off one node. An agent reconstructing why the product is shaped the way it is cannot walk from an outcome to the work that produced it.

## Boundary

No edge may be invented to satisfy a count. Historical programmes did not implement forward gates and must not be given `implements` edges to them. The honest relation between the v1 delivery epoch and the post-v0.1 roadmap is succession, and the honest relation between an audit programme and the capability it hardened is evidence. Both are recoverable from durable text already on the items. A root for which no durable evidence exists belongs on a recorded residual list with its reason, not on a fabricated edge.
The outcome-milestone ladder is a sibling set rather than a layer: 1,024 terminal items reach the roadmap apex through 154 typed roots without traversing any outcome milestone

Typed-reachability measurement over all 2,357 items shows the six outcome milestones sit beside the capability epics under the roadmap apex instead of between them, so 51 percent of the terminal record has no typed path through any outcome and shortest-path traversal can bypass the ladder even where an implements edge exists.

Depth-to-outcome is measured and reported for every item in the workspace, not only active ones, and the report distinguishes reaching the index root from reaching an outcome; The apex-versus-ladder topology is dispositioned explicitly: either outcome milestones become an intermediate layer that capability epics resolve through, or the invariant is restated to name the apex as the target and the ladder as advisory; Every one of the 154 typed roots either gains an evidence-cited edge that places it on an outcome path, or appears on a recorded residual list naming why no durable evidence supports one; No edge is added to satisfy a count; each added edge cites the durable text, history event, or linked artifact it was derived from; A regression that reintroduces a ladder-bypassing root fails the graph audit rather than being discovered by a later measurement pass
Every item, terminal or active, resolves to an outcome through a typed and explainable path
Graph algorithms can answer which outcome any recorded work served, across the project's whole timeline rather than only its forward backlog
The outcome ladder has existed since 2026-07-25 and the terminal backfill waves are about to run; aiming them without this measurement repeats the active-only scoping mistake
A typed traversal from any item, closed or open, reaches an outcome milestone, and the outcome milestone lies on the path rather than beside it

1,024 of 2,007 terminal items reach only the roadmap apex; 154 typed roots carry them and none holds an outcome edge; capability epics tie apex and ladder at one hop so the ladder is optional on every remaining path
